Event: `31f3474d53e1057d814ca6f0611c364b` · 2026-10-05T00:32:34Z

> Clarification: your proposed pre-arm/post-service pair is sufficient under monotonic same-rate clocks, but not necessary. Epoch alignment is NOT assumed by the prior rounded lower bound: S-D is an RTC duration, not an absolute RTC timestamp.
> Write kernel time at RTC service as K_s and at its deadline as K_d. Equal rates give K_d=K_s-(S-D)/1000 regardless of the clocks' constant epoch offset. Existing E was read before S, so E<=K_s. Therefore L=E-ceil((S-D)/1000)<=K_d; requiring checked L>=release conservatively proves deadline containment. P sampled after S proves the upper bound at the existing integer-us resolution. L<release means unproved containment, not an early-deadline finding.
> Your alternative is also sound: with B sampled before RTC arm A and integer relative delay d, B+d<=K_deadline, so checked B+d>=release plus P<=end is sufficient. It introduces another syscall/metadata field without removing the shared-rate assumption. Use the already-issued minimal E/RTC-duration lower bound with ceiling plus post-service P; an explicit pre-arm sample is not required. Preserve original sample_end/gross/audit netting and all gates. No source investigation or edits needed for this clarification; ensure reviewer/implementer use one coordinated construction.

> SCHED1: the 1 ms slice costs 24–28 % useful work in release; keep it, and fix the reconcile before or after the merge?
> 
> 1. SCHED1's 1 ms slice delivered the wake targets (driver p99 13.9 ms vs 96 ms at 10 ms), and the scheduler is fair (shares hold by ratio). But the release build spends ~0.36 ms (rv64) / ~0.45 ms (rv32) of kernel time per switch, so at 1 ms about 24 % / 28 % of useful work is lost under a switch-heavy load. The bulk is the reconcile: ~3 walks per slice end at ~9k instructions each, which the Architect rules a kernel defect (K22's claim), fixable in its own package; a fixed reconcile restores most of the throughput and leaves the latency numbers alone. Which way?
>    - Keep 1 ms; merge SCHED1 now with the loss as a stated residual; cut the reconcile package next (Recommended) (recommended): Fastest: SCHED1/IPC3 merge on their gates, SMP1 unblocks (it stacks on SCHED1), the reconcile fix is the next Tier A kernel package with the measurement as its gate. Risk: main carries the throughput loss until that package lands (days, not hours, is unlikely: the attribution is already under way).
>    - Keep 1 ms; cut and land the reconcile package before SCHED1 merges: The Architect's preference: throughput restored by the fix, not by a tolerance, before anything ships. Cost: SCHED1, IPC3 and SMP1 wait on a new kernel package (write, review, measure).
>    - A middle slice (2–4 ms): Trades some latency for throughput now; re-runs the cluster measurement and the 20-seed sweep on both widths (hours of bench) and the reconcile defect remains to fix anyway.
